title: The Labyrinth of Form
text:
Postmodern fiction often resists the notion of a single, authoritative narrator. Instead, it fragments its voice across multiple perspectives, footnotes, and deliberately unreliable accounts. Writers such as Italo Calvino and Jorge Luis Borges exploited this instability to question whether any text can faithfully represent reality. The reader is thus compelled to assemble meaning from ruptured fragments rather than receive it passively.

Experimental novels of the mid-twentieth century frequently embedded games, labyrinths, and self-referential structures within their narratives. Critics have argued that these devices expose the artificiality of literary conventions rather than merely decorating them. Such works, though often dismissed as impenetrable, reward patient readers who are willing to tolerate ambiguity. Their difficulty, in other words, is itself a form of meaning.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, what does postmodern fiction often resist?
According to the second paragraph, what do critics argue experimental devices do?
options: They expose the artificiality of literary conventions
They make novels easier to read

questions.text: What does the author imply about readers of postmodern texts?
options: They should expect a single, stable meaning
They must actively construct meaning themselves
They are generally unable to understand experimental works
They prefer conventional narratives to fragmented ones

questions.text: Why does the author suggest that the difficulty of experimental works might be meaningful?
options: Because it proves the works are poorly written
Because difficulty itself communicates something about the nature of meaning
Because critics demand it from all novelists
Because the authors wished to discourage readers

paragraph_translations: La ficción posmoderna a menudo se resiste a la noción de un narrador único y autoritario. En cambio, fragmenta su voz entre múltiples perspectivas, notas al pie y relatos deliberadamente poco fiables. Escritores como Italo Calvino y Jorge Luis Borges explotaron esta inestabilidad para cuestionar si algún texto puede representar fielmente la realidad. Así, el lector se ve obligado a armar el significado a partir de fragmentos rotos en lugar de recibirlo pasivamente.

Las novelas experimentales de mediados del siglo XX incorporaban con frecuencia juegos, laberintos y estructuras autorreferenciales dentro de sus narraciones. Los críticos han sostenido que estos recursos exponen la artificialidad de las convenciones literarias en lugar de limitarse a decorarlas. Estas obras, aunque a menudo descartadas como impenetrables, recompensan a los lectores pacientes dispuestos a tolerar la ambigüedad. Su dificultad, en otras palabras, es en sí misma una forma de significado.
